High-level design

Project MCS · registry v0.2.0 · generated 2026-11-23 · build 576b15da · owner Aviral

1. Context and goals

Matsui's customers contact support for FAQs, troubleshooting, ticket/AMC status, spare parts and quotes. This POC shows a low-latency hybrid multi-agent service desk for email and chat that:

  1. answers routine requests from rules and caches in milliseconds (no large model on the hot path),
  2. reasons over product knowledge with KG-RAG for multi-hop troubleshooting,
  3. checks answers for grounding before they leave the system, and
  4. hands off to humans with full context when confidence is low or safety is involved.

Success metrics (from the registry): T0/T1 p95 under 300 ms and at least 50% fast-path share (NFR-PERF-01, NFR-PERF-03); groundedness at least 0.90 and zero fabricated answers on unknowns (NFR-QUAL-01); routing accuracy at least 90% (NFR-QUAL-02); measurable multi-hop gain of hybrid KG-RAG over vector RAG (NFR-QUAL-03).

2. Scope and constraints

In this POC Later
Channels Chat widget (SSE), email (built-in demo mailbox + Gmail API adapter), contact form Voice (STT/TTS on the chat fast path), WhatsApp
Knowledge Synthetic manuals, policies, FAQs, catalog, KG; runtime uploads Real Matsui manuals, ERP/CRM connectors
Users Customers (demo personas), agents, admins SSO with Matsui IdP
Attachments Stored and shown to humans AI parsing (photos of nameplates, PDFs)

Constraints: Google Cloud for every environment, no local Docker (D-015); one developer with Claude Code; all data synthetic and labelled as demo (DR-03); the core must be channel-agnostic so voice can reuse it (BR-05).

3.1 Channels and adapters

Each channel has an adapter that converts native input into one message envelope (channel, conversation id, customer identity, text, attachments, metadata) and renders the orchestrator's output back into the channel format (FR-OR-01).

  • Chat: the widget opens a session and streams the reply over SSE (status, tokens, citations, quick actions, forms, handoff events) (FR-CH-01).
  • Email: an InboundMailAdapter has two implementations: a built-in demo mailbox (Postgres inbox/outbox shown in the console) for dev, tests and offline demos, and a Gmail API adapter for a real demo inbox (Pub/Sub push notifications to Cloud Run; replies sent through the Gmail API) (D-016). It threads by Message-ID/References and by the ticket reference in the subject (FR-EM-01). The help-centre contact form enters the same pipeline (FR-UI-03).
  • Voice (later): an STT → envelope → orchestrator (chat policy) → TTS adapter; no core changes.

3.2 Orchestrator

A code-defined state graph (LangGraph StateGraph) owns the flow. Edges are deterministic Python functions; LLMs only run inside specific nodes (FR-OR-02, D-001). The orchestrator:

  • keeps conversation state: active specialist, extracted entities (model, serial, error code, city), open slots, last evidence (FR-CH-02),
  • applies the channel policy profile (latency budget, verification mode, auto-send threshold, allowed tiers) (FR-OR-04),
  • decomposes multi-question emails into sub-queries answered in parallel and merges them (FR-EM-02),
  • enforces per-node timeouts and falls back gracefully (FR-OR-06).

An LLM supervisor is used only where it pays off: the T3 planner for messy multi-intent requests and the email path, where latency is not user-facing.

3.3 Tiered cascade and router

flowchart LR
  IN[Envelope] --> GR[Guardrails<br/>safety · injection · OOS]
  GR -->|safety| P1[P1 handoff + safety text]
  GR --> RL[Rule layer<br/>regex entities · exact intents]
  RL -->|ticket id / AMC id / human| T0
  RL --> KNN[Embedding kNN intent]
  KNN -->|conf ≥ 0.80| D{Dispatch}
  KNN -->|low conf| LLM[Fast-LLM router · JSON]
  LLM --> D
  D --> T0[T0 tools/forms]
  D --> C[T1 exact → semantic cache]
  C -->|miss| T2[T2 RAG]
  D --> T3[T3 specialists]
  T2 -->|abstain / low score| T3
Tier Handles Mechanism LLM calls Target p95
T0 Greetings, ticket/AMC/warranty lookup, create ticket, talk to human, safety Regex + dictionaries + typed tools + slot-filling FSM 0 under 300 ms
T1 Public FAQs and paraphrases Exact normalized-text cache, then semantic FAQ cache (cos ≥ 0.90) 0 (1 embedding) under 300 ms
T2 Single-hop knowledge questions Hybrid retrieval + rerank + one fast-model call with citations 1 first token under 1.2 s
T3 Multi-hop troubleshooting, parts + stock + coverage, multi-intent Specialist agents with KG-RAG + tools 1–3 first token under 2.5 s
T4 Low confidence, safety, angry escalation, explicit request Human queue (chat) / review queue (email) 1 (summary) —

The router itself is a cascade (FR-RT-01 → FR-RT-02 → FR-RT-03): most traffic is resolved by rules and the embedding classifier; only ambiguous messages pay for the small-LLM router. Retrieval starts in parallel with routing (speculative) so context is ready when T2/T3 begin.

3.4 Specialist agents and tools

Agent Responsibility Main tools / data Pattern
Troubleshooting Diagnose error codes and symptoms; customer-safe steps first; offer service request KG templates (diagnose, shared causes), manual chunks Handoff-capable specialist (FR-AG-01)
Service request Create ticket: serial, issue, contact; rule-based priority create_ticket, asset lookup, inline form Deterministic FSM, LLM only for slot extraction (FR-AG-02)
Account lookups Ticket, asset, warranty, AMC status Postgres tools, customer-scoped T0 tools (FR-AG-03)
Parts Compatible part, price, stock per warehouse, lead time, quote request KG STOCKED_AT, FITS, create_parts_quote Specialist (FR-AG-04)
Sales lead Capture quote requests and route to sales create_lead Specialist (FR-AG-05)

In chat, the active specialist stays sticky across turns (handoff/swarm pattern), so follow-ups skip routing unless the rule layer detects an intent switch (FR-OR-05). Tools enforce that records belong to the identified customer (FR-AG-06).

3.5 Knowledge layer: RAG, KG and hybrid

Two complementary stores:

  • Document index (Postgres + pgvector + FTS): policies, manuals, bulletins, chunked by heading with tables and error-code sections kept whole (FR-RG-02). Hybrid lexical + vector retrieval with RRF, metadata filters and reranking (FR-RG-01, FR-RG-03, FR-RG-04). Superseded versions are excluded (FR-RG-06).
  • Product knowledge graph (Neo4j): Model → ErrorCode → Cause → Resolution → SparePart → Warehouse, plus components, service centres, AMC coverage and documents (FR-KG-01).

Why both: questions like "Our DHD-150 shows E04 — which part do we need and is it in stock in Pune, and is it covered by Platinum AMC?" need 4–5 hops across entities. Vector RAG tends to retrieve the right manual section but cannot reliably join stock and coverage; the KG answers the joins exactly and points back to the manual chunk for the explanation (FR-KG-05).

GraphRAG strategy (D-006): link entities → run parameterized Cypher templates for known patterns (fast, safe) → fall back to guarded Text2Cypher for the long tail (FR-KG-02, FR-KG-03, FR-KG-04). Customer data stays in Postgres and is accessed through tools, not the graph.

Benchmark: the eval harness runs RAG-only, KG-only and hybrid on the labelled set (183 items, 1–5 hops) to give a reproducible comparison (FR-KG-06, DR-02).

3.6 Verification and hallucination control

Layer Check Chat Email
Prompting Cite evidence ids for every claim; abstain when unsupported (FR-RG-05) sync sync
Rules Citation coverage per sentence (FR-VF-01); part numbers, prices, codes, ticket ids exist in DB/KG (FR-VF-03) sync (~20 ms) sync
LLM judge Faithfulness score 0–1 against evidence (FR-VF-02) async on 20% sample (FR-VF-05) sync
Decision Confidence = f(router, retrieval, verifier, flags) vs channel threshold (FR-VF-04) handoff below threshold draft to review below threshold (FR-EM-03)

Retrieved text is always treated as data, never as instructions (FR-RT-05). Runtime-upload eval items double as a hallucination test: before upload the system must abstain.

3.7 Human handoff and agent console

Handoff triggers: safety signals (FR-RT-04), low confidence, explicit request, repeated complaint/escalation, policy flags. The human receives an AI-generated handoff summary (FR-HO-04) and a workspace with conversation, customer/asset/AMC context and the AI trace (FR-HO-02). Chat supports live take-over and return to bot; email drafts are edited and sent from the review queue (FR-HO-01, FR-HO-03). Good answers can be promoted to the FAQ cache (FR-CA-05).

3.8 Knowledge operations and runtime upload

flowchart LR
  U[Admin upload] -->|doc: md/pdf/docx/txt| J[(jobs)]
  U -->|csv: error_codes / parts / faqs| V[Schema validation]
  J --> P[Parse → chunk → embed → index]
  P --> X[LLM graph extraction<br/>schema-constrained]
  X -->|conf ≥ τ| KG[(Neo4j)]
  X -->|conf < τ| Q[KG change requests<br/>approve / reject]
  Q --> KG
  V --> PG[(Postgres)]
  V --> KG
  P --> PG
  P --> INV[Invalidate cache entries citing changed docs]

Uploads are processed by a background worker without restarts (FR-KB-01, FR-KB-02). Document extraction proposes KG changes with provenance and confidence (FR-KB-03). New versions supersede old ones (FR-KB-05), and dependent cache entries are invalidated (FR-CA-03). The admin UI shows jobs, documents, FAQ entries and pending graph changes (FR-KB-04).

3.9 User interface architecture

UI inspiration is Zendesk (clean, neutral, card-based, help-centre search hero, chat-widget mockup), re-themed with Matsui identity: navy and Matsui blue, white surfaces, industrial product photography, and the tagline "Total Solution Provider in Auxiliary Equipment for Plastic Processing" (FR-UI-07).

Surface Audience Key elements
Help centre Customers Hero search · 7 product-family cards · popular articles · service bulletins · contact strip (email form, chat, breakdown line) (FR-UI-01)
Article page Customers Heading anchors (citation targets), version badge, related articles (FR-UI-02)
Chat widget Customers Streaming answer, status line ("Checking the DHD-150 troubleshooting guide…"), citation chips, quick replies, inline forms, human takeover (FR-CH-03–FR-CH-05)
Agent console Agents Three panes: views · conversation · context + AI trace (FR-UI-04)
Knowledge admin Admins Upload, jobs, documents, FAQ cache, KG changes, KG explorer (FR-UI-05)
Analytics Leadership Tier mix, latency per tier, deflection, groundedness, cost, RAG vs KG benchmark (FR-UI-06)
Demo bar Presenter Persona switch, reset, send sample emails (FR-UI-08)

4.3 Latency budget (chat)

Step T0/T1 path T3 path
Guardrails + rule layer 5–10 ms 5–10 ms
Query embedding (shared by cache, kNN router, retrieval) 30–60 ms 30–60 ms
kNN intent + cache lookup 5–15 ms 5–15 ms
Small-LLM router (only if low confidence) — +300–600 ms
Tool / DB lookup 10–50 ms —
Entity linking + KG templates (parallel with vector search) — 50–120 ms
Rerank — 80–150 ms
Status event to client — under 500 ms
Generation first token (fast/strong model) — 0.8–1.5 s
Sync rule verification 5 ms 20 ms
Total under 300 ms first token 1.5–2.5 s, complete under 6 s

Email budget is 60 s end to end, which allows the planner, the strong model and the synchronous judge (NFR-PERF-02). Token cost is logged per request (NFR-COST-01).

4.4 Security and privacy

  • Identity: staff use Google sign-in with roles (agent, admin) (NFR-SEC-01). Chat customers are anonymous or demo personas. Email senders are matched by contact email, then domain; unknown senders get public answers only (FR-EM-04).
  • Least privilege for AI: typed tool allow-list, customer scope checks, read-only DB and graph users, guarded Text2Cypher, no raw SQL from models (NFR-SEC-03, FR-AG-06, FR-KG-04).
  • Injection and exfiltration: input screening, documents treated as data, refusal to reveal system prompts or other customers' data (FR-RT-05); caches never hold personal answers (FR-CA-04).
  • Privacy: PII masked in logs (FR-RT-06); 30-day retention with a purge job (NFR-SEC-04); secrets in .env/Secret Manager (NFR-SEC-02).

5. Deployment architecture

Everything runs on Google Cloud; developers need only gcloud, Python 3.12 (uv) and Node 20 (pnpm) — no local Docker (D-015, NFR-DEP-01). Two environments share one design: dev (cheap tiers, used while building) and demo (sized and warmed for presentations). Images are built remotely by Cloud Build (NFR-DEP-02); make seed loads mock data into the dev services (FR-KB-06).

Region asia-south1 (Mumbai) for latency to Indian users. Min instances = 1 on the API in demo to avoid cold starts; dev scales to zero to save cost.

6. Important design decisions

Mirrored in DECISIONS.md. Traceability is enforced in CI (NFR-MNT-01).

ID Decision Rationale Alternatives considered
D-001 Code-based orchestrator (LangGraph state graph); an LLM supervisor only inside T3 planning and email Deterministic, ms-level routing; LLM supervisor adds 1–2 sequential calls per turn LLM supervisor for everything; pure ReAct single agent
D-002 Tiered cascade T0–T4 with early exit and speculative retrieval Pays for big models only when needed; voice-ready fast path Single RAG path for all queries
D-003 Python/FastAPI for the agent service; Next.js/TypeScript for web Strongest ecosystem for LangGraph, rerankers, document parsing, Neo4j GraphRAG; Node kept for the UI Node/TS end to end (as in the portal POC)
D-004 Postgres + pgvector for relational data, vectors, FTS, cache and traces One store keeps the POC simple and transactional; good enough at demo scale Dedicated vector DB, Redis cache
D-005 Neo4j for the knowledge graph Cypher, full-text indexes, mature Python driver, GraphRAG tooling Postgres recursive CTEs, Apache AGE
D-006 GraphRAG = templates first, guarded Text2Cypher fallback; KG holds product knowledge only Fast and safe for known patterns; customer data stays behind scoped tools Text2Cypher only; KG-only answers
D-007 Semantic cache only for curated public answers (τ = 0.90) with source-doc invalidation Prevents stale or personal answers being served from cache Cache all LLM answers
D-008 Sync rule checks everywhere; LLM judge sync for email, async sampled for chat Keeps chat latency low while still auditing grounding Judge on every chat turn
D-009 ~~Mailpit for dev email~~ — superseded by D-016 — —
D-010 SSE for chat streaming and console live updates Works on Cloud Run, simple to proxy, enough for one-way streams WebSockets
D-011 Postgres job table + worker instead of Pub/Sub Fewer moving parts for a POC; same interface can move to Cloud Tasks Pub/Sub, Celery + Redis
D-012 Deterministic synthetic data generator with an eval set Reproducible demos and benchmarks; no real customer data Hand-written fixtures
D-013 Provider-agnostic LLM layer; fast model for router/T2, strong model for T3/judge Swap models after the latency/cost bake-off Hard-wire one vendor
D-014 Docs as code: JSON registry + build steps → generated HTML with CI trace gate Traceability without manual sync Hand-maintained HTML
D-015 GCP-first, no local Docker: managed dev services (Cloud SQL, AuraDB Free, GCS, Vertex) + native app processes; Cloud Build for CI and images; Cloud Run for dev and demo Developer has no Docker; keeps dev identical to the demo platform Docker Compose locally
D-016 Email via adapter: built-in demo mailbox (Postgres) + Gmail API with Pub/Sub push; Mailpit dropped Works without Docker; Cloud Run accepts only HTTP so an SMTP sink can't run there Mailpit, SendGrid inbound parse

8. Risks

Risk Impact Mitigation
LLM latency variance on Cloud Run / provider Chat feels slow Fast path T0/T1, status events, streaming, timeouts with fallback, min instances
Hallucinated part numbers or prices Wrong orders, trust loss Entity/number consistency rules against DB/KG; citations; abstention
KG extraction errors from uploads Wrong multi-hop answers Schema-constrained extraction, confidence threshold, approval queue, provenance for rollback
Synthetic data feels unrealistic to Matsui Weak demo Product categories mirror the real range; swap in real manuals early
Scope creep (voice, ERP) Delays Voice-ready core but voice out of scope; ERP mocked
Neo4j hosting cost/ops Budget AuraDB Free in dev; small VM or AuraDB for demo; KG is small
Dev depends on cloud services No offline work; small running cost Smallest tiers, dev scales to zero, FakeProvider for unit tests, budget alert on the project
